links.targetTitle: Pattern operates on borrowed USDS: minting draws vault debt

title: Obex's operating capital is debt minted against a Sky Allocation Vault, not assets the Agent owns
content:
A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.1.1 describes minting as drawing "USDS from the **Sky Allocation Vault** to the Obex ALM Proxy": the contract mints into the buffer contract, then transfers from buffer to proxy. Burning is described as the inverse — the relayer "return[s] and then burn[s] **Obex's USDS debt** in the Sky Allocation Vault," and the contract will "burn the USDS from the buffer and `wipe` an equivalent amount from the vault's debt" (A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.1.2.1). The vault is named at A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.1.1.4.1 as `ALLOCATOR-OBEX-A`.

So the capital Obex deploys is borrowed into existence against a vault Sky controls. The Agent is a leveraged operator of ecosystem credit, not a fund investing its own balance sheet — every position it holds has a corresponding USDS liability.

This reframes several other provisions. The mint rate limit is a debt ceiling on the Agent's velocity of borrowing. The Encumbrance Ratio commitment (A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.1.3.1) is a leverage constraint on that borrowing. And the Freezer's mandate to act when Obex breaches Risk Capital or ALM rules is a creditor's remedy — Sky is the counterparty whose money is at risk when the Agent misjudges.

It also explains why the emergency runbook terminates in `burnUSDS`. Unwinding an Obex position is not selling assets and holding cash; it is retiring debt, returning the system to the state it was in before the Agent borrowed. The Agent's liquidity is a loan with a defined repayment path, and the repayment path is the emergency plan.
description: mintUSDS draws newly minted USDS from the Sky Allocation Vault through a buffer into the ALM Proxy, and burnUSDS wipes an equivalent amount of the vault's debt.
